column1: Client onboarding to verified booking

column1: Shoot request to final delivery

column1: First draft to useful coach to revision

column9: The shared-login test set meets the pilot attribution target or remains visibly unconfirmed.

column1: Designer research to applied improvement

column8: An active ad or engagement count is not a lead/booking result. Unlicensed references cannot become client assets. Many saved references do not earn automatic score credit.

column9: Report totals match the source period and every creative row points to the approved asset version.

column8: Retrying a webhook creates one lead. Missing CRM stages cannot become zero conversions. Conflicting/cancelled bookings are reconciled before reporting.

column8: A stale card cannot override a newer answer. Paperclip outage retains retries. A done decision is not resent solely because an old spec says open.
column9: The owner decides on Telegram and the source task shows the same answer with its dependency state reconciled.

column8: Unconfirmed suggested action items remain proposals. Forwarding a message cannot widen its audience. Chat text never changes a person score.
column9: Retrying confirmation produces one accepted task with a clear next action and original instruction provenance.

column4: Someone deliberately submits meeting notes or a voice note
column5: COM-106 COM-107 COM-109 COM-111 COM-114 COM-117

column8: Low-confidence names/dates request clarification. Recording without permission stays disabled. Model suggestions cannot commit client promises.
column9: A confirmed action is traceable to reviewed notes and has a responsible owner; notes-only capture remains usable.

column8: Unapproved changes cannot silently expand a creator target. Conflicting client stakeholders are routed to the authorised approver. Prior work keeps its provenance.
column9: The new delivery target explains exactly which approved scope change moved it and who accepted the impact.

column1: Employee correction to rebuilt weekly score
column4: A person disputes delivery credit, context or a score
column5: TRK-136 PRF-007 PRF-034 PRF-035 CORE-137

column8: A denied case includes a reason and appeal route. Downstream cached reports cannot retain the superseded number as current. Managers cannot retaliate through hidden score changes.
column9: The person sees a resolved case and the same corrected figure wherever the current weekly score appears.

column1: Hiring requisition to first delivery
column3: Hiring manager, HR, candidate, buddy, PGS
column4: A capacity gap becomes an approved hiring request

column7: Requisition, human hiring decision, accepted offer link, readiness checklist, first-delivery receipt
column8: Incomplete documents/setup keep the person unready rather than lowering performance. Candidate data has separate scope and retention; no automated hiring rejection or KYC copying.
column9: The first delivery belongs to the new person, uses the correct permissions and meets an agreed ramp benchmark.

column1: Leave request to payroll hand-off
column3: Employee, pod lead, HR, payroll provider
column4: A person requests time off in a payroll period
column6: Preview eligibility and balance; apply and approve with coverage/delegation; update the balance ledger, calendar and availability; reconcile day statuses at period close; approve the payroll input export and match the provider acknowledgement
column7: Leave decision, ledger entries, day statuses, export batch/hash, provider reconciliation
column8: Concurrent approval cannot double-debit balance. A post-cutoff change becomes a correction batch. Payroll calculation and statutory filings stay with the qualified provider.
column9: Approved leave appears once in balances/calendar and the acknowledged payroll input, without exposing salaries to pod leads.

column1: Attendance exception to corrected day status
column4: Desktop/calendar/check-in signals disagree or are absent
column6: Use the published source precedence; build a daily suggestion from permitted sources and approved leave; ask the person to reconcile missing evidence; approve a correction and close the period; export daily statuses with source-health context
column7: Day status, source coverage, employee explanation, approved correction, close receipt
column8: Missing telemetry never proves absence. Calendar busy time does not prove work. HR cannot inspect raw minute timelines, and no camera input exists.
column9: HR sees one explainable status per day and the employee can correct it before payroll cut-off.

column1: New project to ready task and available assignee
column3: Sales, PGS, creator, HR availability service
column4: A new work package is approved
column5: PRJ-004 PRJ-014 PRJ-041 PRJ-042 HR-076 AST-055

column7: Project/task IDs, readiness checklist, available-capacity snapshot, accepted commitment
column8: Unavailable or unready people are not silently assigned. Missing inputs make a blocker. A later leave change triggers a reviewed replan rather than an unexplained missed target.
column9: The assignee receives a ready task with a scoped brief and a realistic approved date.

column4: A workload cluster or support request indicates capacity risk
column5: PRF-161 PRF-162 PRF-167 PRF-168 HR-076 PRJ-092

column7: Demand snapshot, capacity assumptions, support request, reviewed assignment changes, follow-through
column8: The system does not diagnose burnout from activity or rank people. New deadlines require actual acceptance. Keep private wellbeing notes out of resourcing projections.
column9: A support request results in a named intervention and updated commitments that the affected people can see.

column1: Monthly evidence to human appraisal to growth plan
column4: An agreed review cycle starts
column6: Freeze delivery/skill/quality evidence with scope and sufficiency; let the employee preview and correct it; collect human assessments and calibrate rubric use; hold the review and record acknowledgement/dissent; agree a development plan with work-linked practice
column7: Frozen evidence packet, corrections, human review reasons, acknowledgement, growth actions
column8: Insufficient data is labelled, not scored as failure. Scores do not automatically set increments. Restricted compensation recommendations use separate authority and channels.
column9: The employee can trace each review claim, challenge it and see an agreed supported growth action.

column1: Offboarding to access closure and project continuity
column4: An approved exit date is recorded
column5: HR-089 HR-090 HR-091 HR-093 CORE-035 CORE-109 CORE-171

column7: Exit checklist, handover receipts, revocation evidence, asset exceptions, final-input batch
column8: A failed revocation is a blocking security exception. Personal account ownership cannot be fixed by moving files without authority. Legal hold protects only its justified scope.
column9: An exited person cannot access current data through APIs, devices or caches, and every active project has a new accountable owner.

column4: Collector lag, token expiry or permission failure is detected

column1: Process bottleneck to measured improvement
column4: Repeated waiting or rework motivates a process review

column8: A missing event is not proof of delay or blame. Observational change does not establish causation. Do not repurpose private activity/chat for process scoring.
column9: The team can explain a bottleneck and measure a chosen process change without a worker ranking.

column9: Every launch claim traces to permitted dated evidence and the client sees uncertainty before choosing.
